cur:objects-monasterboice-west-cross.summary: This very tall, slender cross stands beside the ruined church at Monasterboice; its west face is divided into panels of scriptural scenes, with the Crucifixion at the centre of the ringed head. Christ is shown on the cross with arms outstretched, in the tradition of the Irish high crosses that place the saving death of Christ at the very heart of the cross. Weathering has softened the carving, but the whole programme still leads the eye upward to the crucified Lord.
facts: Monasterboice has three high crosses, the North, West and South (Muiredach's) crosses; Wikipedia notes that the North and West crosses have suffered much more from weathering than Muiredach's Cross.
On Irish 'scripture' crosses the west face usually carries New Testament scenes, with the Crucifixion in the centre of the head (type).
